clue.text: One who's swotted excessively, back to front in schools

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the word is shifted round to stand at its front

blocks.note: a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod

explanation.surface: Describing a pupil who crammed far too hard at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sits between definition and wordplay: the wordplay is PODS with its last letter brought to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A spod is British slang for a dull, studious person, a swot or nerd.

clue.text: Exhausted, rowers caught tucking in like much of what's in larder

definitions.text: like much of what's in larder

indicators.note: something tucking in is put inside, so the rowers and catch go into the word for exhausted

blocks.note: a rowing team is a crew
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Tired oarsmen tuck into food, like the provisions stocked in a pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowers and the catch slip in after the first letter of the exhausted word, not around it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Many jars and bottles kept in a larder are sealed with screw caps, so they are screwcapped.

clue.text: Shape in advance head of putter, capital club

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the Reform Club is a gentlemen's club in London, the capital

explanation.surface: A golfer chooses a putter as the lead club in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To preform is to give something its shape beforehand, ahead of the final moulding.

clue.text: Explosive number I eulogize, given a lift

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the letters makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A performer offers praise for a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: N I LAUD read upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualin is a dynamite-like explosive made with nitroglycerine and sawdust.

clue.text: Scramble for Scotch? Positive shake after second

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Mixing a whisky cocktail, you give the shaker a firm rattle after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after second' puts S first; the question mark flags that the definition means the Scots word, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprattle is a Scots dialect verb meaning to scramble or struggle.

clue.text: Very good tin rings for plough

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
pi is slang for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A shiny tin of something is wanted for the farmer's plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' is not farming here: it is old British university slang for failing an exam candidate, as is spin.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British university slang, to plough or spin a candidate is to fail them in an exam.

clue.text: Party nipped by farm animal, a pariah

indicators.note: something nipped is gripped between jaws, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: a pig is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A guest at a farmyard party gets bitten by an animal and shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pi-dog or pye-dog is a stray, ownerless dog of Asia, also called a pariah dog.

clue.text: Purifies, sin-free, with conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into a new form, here a new letter order

explanation.surface: A religious conversion leaves the believer cleansed and free of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to remove its impurities, so refines and purifies are synonyms.

clue.text: Red wine, one litre bottled, a gift

indicators.note: something bottled is held inside a container, so these letters go inside the wine

blocks.note: one is the indefinite article a
L is the abbreviation for litre
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A litre of red wine in a bottle makes a nice present.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red wine from Spain, often used for communion.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, often called a gift.

clue.text: Head round racecourse with useless ruse one plotted

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the second piece sits inside the first
read as use-less: the word loses the letters u, s, e

blocks.note: tête is French for head, used in English for a headdress
Chambers gives rink as a course for racing, for skaters or curlers
the word minus u, s and e

explanation.surface: The man in charge of a racecourse uses a futile trick, a plotter at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'useless' as use-less: ruse without its u, s and e. Tête is French for head, also used in English for a tall headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinketer is an old word for one who intrigues or has secret dealings, a schemer.

clue.text: Bit of money in island state (a rial's different)

definitions.text: Bit of money in island state

indicators.note: made different, the letters are set into a new order

explanation.surface: An island nation's coin differs from the rial used elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The island state is the Maldives; the rial is the currency of Iran and Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: The laari is a coin of the Maldives, one hundredth of a rufiyaa.

clue.text: Dealer: publisher has one calling round

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

explanation.surface: A publishing house employs a town crier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' reads as the publisher holding the crier, but it is the crier going round the publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier is the casino employee who deals cards and runs a gaming table.

clue.text: Dog having to t-tear away in the lead, one ahead of the pack?

indicators.note: being in the lead means going in front, so this piece is placed first

blocks.note: a stuttered T- followed by rend, to tear away
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A dog keen to tear off at the front of a hunting pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the lead' places the stuttered tearing before the dog; 'pack' suggests hounds but means the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A trendsetter starts fashions before everyone else, so is ahead of the crowd.

clue.text: Cleared nappy from behind

indicators.note: reading from behind means starting at the end and working to the start

blocks.note: diaper is the American word for nappy

explanation.surface: A baby's backside has been cleaned up after a soiled nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that has been repaid has been cleared, settled in full.

clue.text: Like leaves with respect to limiting return of indisposition

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
to limit something is to set bounds around it, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Talking of plants, an illness keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliar is the botanical adjective meaning of or relating to leaves.

clue.text: Financially sound but left out, is model of industry nominal?

indicators.note: left can be L, and leaving it out means removing that letter

blocks.note: the ant is the proverbial model of hard work

explanation.surface: Asking whether a business that's solvent but excluded is only a showcase in name.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLID loses its L. The ant appears in Proverbs as an example of industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Soi-disant, French for self-styled, means so-called, in name only.

clue.text: Oxygen respirators will include this kind

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within them, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Breathing equipment that supplies oxygen comes as a type of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind or category, especially of art or literature.

clue.text: Paying court to fix wig on? Nothing included

indicators.note: being included means being brought inside the rest of the letters
to fix can mean to arrange or doctor, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vain suitor straightens his wig before courting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing is courting someone romantically, the present participle matching paying court.

clue.text: Grandma and family in cotton cloth

blocks.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny and relatives dressed in cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankin, or nankeen, is a buff-coloured cotton cloth originally made in Nanking.

clue.text: Small wired petticoat French girl put round centre of midriff, fashionable

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so that one alone is kept
placed around the other letters so they sit inside

blocks.note: Colette is a French girl's name, and the French novelist

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman wears a fashionable slip around her waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The French girl is Colette, also the name of the French novelist; she wraps around everything but her opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinolette is a small crinoline, a petticoat stiffened with wire or hoops to hold the skirt out.

clue.text: Bad news in the stables to clobber somebody (not on)

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken away, here those two letters

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: Grim news reaches the yard that someone is to get a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSON drops ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampers, or lampas, is a swelling of the roof of a horse's mouth, so unwelcome in a stable.

clue.text: You may find gleeman in one

definitions.text: You may find gleeman in one

indicators.note: the thing defined is a jumble, so inside it the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A medieval minstrel might turn up in a mixed crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-referential: the jumbled letters of gleeman make the word for a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A mélange is a mixture or medley, the very thing that holds the scrambled letters.

clue.text: Ruins god imposed on nations

indicators.note: in an across entry, something imposed on another is laid on top, so it comes first

blocks.note: a deva is a god in Hindu and Buddhist belief

explanation.surface: A deity's rule brought down on whole countries wrecks them.
explanation.walkthrough: A deva is a divine being in Hindu and Buddhist belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastates means wrecks or lays waste, the verb sense of ruins.

clue.text: Line cast in river to catch predator

blocks.note: ea is a dialect word for a river

explanation.surface: An angler casts a line into the river hoping to land a pike.
explanation.walkthrough: EA is Chambers' dialect word for a river, a favourite of barred-puzzle setters.
explanation.definitionFit: The elanet is a kite, a bird of prey, so a predator.

clue.text: A blue achieving something unique in excellence

blocks.note: perse is a dark greyish-blue colour

explanation.walkthrough: A blue is a university sportsman's award, but here it is just a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An a-per-se is a person or thing that is the very best, unrivalled in its excellence.

clue.text: Short letter (epistolary): I help when unravelling marks

indicators.note: unravelled threads come loose from their order, and so do these letters

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the Epistle to Philemon in the New Testament, whose abbreviated title this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Philem. is the standard short form for Philemon, a letter or epistle of Paul.

clue.text: I do declare there's nothing lower than the underworld

clue.text: Wood for furniture one's replaced by copy in auction

clue.text: Deck cleaner, the first person from Marseille appearing in court

blocks.note: to sue is to take to court

clue.text: Festival holds record turns

clue.text: Moggy mush

blocks.note: second meaning: slang for the face

explanation.walkthrough: Moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat; mush is slang for the face, not soft food.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is an everyday word for a cat and also slang for the face or mouth.

clue.text: Fling: second in tangle moving back a bit?

clue.text: Project that's managed in taking oath

indicators.note: the second piece sits within the first

clue.text: Equestrian event: leading character in show has grade adjusted going round

clue.text: Jug: regret once having to go back after end of sentence
